dex._comment: Pokedex page (site/pokedex.html): the site's tile-page size — the single source the on-page pager renders from (read via ROGUE.site().dex.pageSize by site/js/pages/pokedex.js). The in-game Overview draws 28 tiles a page; the site draws 24 (six-up columns with the larger 80px sprites — issue #98), so this is the site's page, not the in-game one.

search._comment: Site-wide search palette (site/js/search-index.js + search.js, and the nav.js header trigger): the trigger's accessible label, the input placeholder, the focused-state 'what to type' hint (shown while the palette is open with an empty query — it never mentions the open shortcut), the open shortcut key, the result cap read by ROGUE.searchQuery, the overflow suffix the count line appends when the query's pre-cap total exceeds the rows shown ({n} = the hidden count), and the scope footer's sentences (issue #152 — what the search covers): scope renders on every page; dexIncluded appends on the Pokédex page, where the species ARE indexed; dexRoute appends on every other page, its {dex} slot filled by a relative link to the Pokédex page (the species-search route).

hero.title: Pokémon Emerald Rogue
hero.subtitle: A roguelite take on Pokémon Emerald: settle into your hub, then head out on a generated run and climb the boss ladder. The guide documents both builds — Vanilla (the gen 1–3 roster) and EX, the expansion build (gen 4–9 plus modern mechanics) — with their differences itemised on the Versions page. New here? Gameplay walks through a first run.

prose.heading: About these docs
prose.text: This is an independent, fan-made field guide to Pokémon Emerald Rogue — an AI-generated reference to the romhack, not affiliated with the romhack's authors. It covers the run loop, the hub, quests, configuration, the Safari Zone, the routes and the mechanics, for both documented builds: Vanilla and EX (the expansion). Game facts are cited per record to the pokeemerald-rogue source on its vanilla and expansion branches; worked examples and commentary are the guide's own, and are labelled as such. New to the game? Gameplay explains a first run; Quests lists the nine quest groups ('Starter Challenges' is currently empty in both builds); Versions compares the two builds.
